title: Choose and apply the licence
body:
The repository is public with no `LICENSE` file, which by default means all rights reserved: nobody may legally copy, use, modify or contribute, and any contribution that arrives has unclear ownership.

**What to add once decided:**

- `LICENSE` with the chosen terms
- `NOTICE` naming the licensor and the work
- A contributor agreement, so the right to relicense later is retained
- A plain-language paragraph in `CONTRIBUTING.md` saying what people may and may not do, without making anyone read the licence to find out
- An ADR recording the reasoning, not just the outcome

**Why it cannot wait.** The direction is one way. A licence can always be loosened later and essentially never tightened, because a version released permissively stays that way and can be forked from forever. The same is true of contributions: once someone else's code is in the tree, changing terms needs their agreement, and one unreachable contributor can freeze the decision permanently.

title: ADR-011: the agentic development environment
body:
The desktop application is about to become an environment that hosts an editor, a file tree and a terminal. `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 2 currently lists the editor as "never replace", and `ADR-003` section 6.2 requires that reversal to be a record rather than a quiet drift.

**The record needs to say:**

- What the surface is, and what it is not
- The one rule: everything the surface shows must be actionable where it is shown
- Why an IDE layout does not make it a dashboard. `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 1 names two failures, the chat box and the dashboard, and neither is about layout. A dashboard is defined by what you cannot do from it
- What is hosted and what is delegated to tools that already exist
- What would reverse the decision

Blocks the first slice of the environment.

title: Plan the environment, sliced
body:
The same shape as `STAGE_0_PLAN` and `STAGE_1_PLAN`: each slice with a build, a proof, and a watch-for.

First slice is the window reading the log, because it is the smallest thing that makes the window worth opening.

Every panel gets the actionable rule applied to it individually, in writing, because that rule is easy to agree with in the abstract and easy to violate one panel at a time.

Depends on ADR-011.

title: Record that a node dials out, never the other way
body:
Consumer machines sit behind NAT and cannot accept inbound connections. This was hit three separate times across both previous projects: by experiment in the NeoEngine peer-to-peer notebooks, again in the old Maschina where a tunnel was the blocker for push notifications, and a third time in the demonstration that actually worked, which used an SSH tunnel rather than any peer connection.

**The rule:** a node opens the connection to the control plane. The control plane never connects to a node.

What is built already satisfies this, which is exactly why it should be written into `06-NODES` now, before Stage 2 makes it load bearing and somebody proposes a callback.

Source: `archaeology/02-LINEAGE.md` sections 3.6 and 7.5.

title: Decide where production Postgres lives
body:
Local development is Docker. `ADR-001` commits to Postgres and not to who runs it.

Blocked on there being anything to host, and on a budget. Kept open so the decision is deliberate rather than made by whoever is closest to a deploy button.

title: Environment: a read path from the window to the control plane
body:
The desktop application currently reads nothing. This is the plumbing every other panel sits on.

**Build.** A read-only client in the Electron main process that talks to the control plane over HTTP, exposed to the renderer through the existing preload bridge. The renderer never speaks to the network or the database directly.

**Done when.** The window displays one real value that came out of the log, and killing the control plane shows a legible error rather than a blank panel.

**Watch for.** The renderer gaining direct network access because it was convenient. `ADR-005` keeps the renderer sandboxed with context isolation on and a locked content security policy, and the boundary check in CI fails the build if the application imports the database package or `pg`.

title: Environment: the log, readable
body:
Events, newest first, with the objective, actor, type and time. The rawest possible view, and the one that proves the read path end to end.

**Done when.** Every event appended by a proof appears in the window without a restart.

**Watch for.** Prettifying the log into something that hides what actually happened. This view is the one place where the record is shown exactly as recorded.

title: Environment: filter and search the log
body:
By objective, actor, type and time range. The same filters the CLI already supports, because anything the CLI can do exists in the control plane API.

**Done when.** The same query typed into the CLI and selected in the window returns the same events.

title: Environment: the objective list
body:
Every objective, its state, and how far along it is. The spine of the whole surface.

**Done when.** An objective stated from the CLI appears in the window, and its state changes as the worker works.

title: Environment: objective detail, with the contract visible
body:
One objective: the statement, the frozen contract with its hash, each criterion and whether it is satisfied, the steps taken, the cost so far.

**Done when.** A criterion satisfied at step two shows as satisfied at step two, from `criterion.satisfied` events, not recomputed at the end.

**Watch for.** Showing a contract that looks editable. It is frozen at admission and changing it creates a new objective. The window must make that obvious rather than implying otherwise.

title: Environment: the queue of things that need a person
body:
`08-ENVIRONMENT` section 1: the primary surface is a queue of things requiring human authority, not a view of things happening. This is the front door, not a side panel.

**Contents.** Suspensions asking a question, approvals for capabilities configured `every_use`, evaluation verdicts that came back indeterminate, and failures that could not be repaired.

**Done when.** The queue is empty when nothing needs a person, and that is the normal state.

**Watch for.** The queue becoming a feed of everything. Most of what Maschina does needs no attention because it is proceeding correctly under granted authority. What needs attention is the residue.

title: Environment: answer a suspended worker's question in place
body:
The first real test of the rule that everything shown is actionable where it is shown.

A stalled worker does not appear as a red dot in a list. It appears as the question it is asking, with a box under it, because slice 7 made that a real object with a real answer.

**Build.** Render the suspension's question, take the answer, record it, resume the worker.

**Done when.** `pnpm stall:live` leaves a worker suspended, the question appears in the window, an answer typed there resumes it, and the whole exchange is in the log.

**Watch for.** An answer that is not recorded as an event. The reply is instruction from the human under their authenticated identity and it is part of the record.

title: Environment: approvals for capabilities configured every_use
body:
A grant that requires approval on every use blocks until a person decides. That decision belongs in the queue with the context needed to make it: who is asking, for what, on what scope, and what it will do.

**Done when.** A capability configured `every_use` blocks a worker, appears in the queue, and approving or denying it from the window releases or refuses the worker, with the denial recorded as prominently as a use.

**Watch for.** An approve button that approves more than the one use in front of it.

title: Environment: verdicts that came back indeterminate
body:
An evaluation that could not decide is not a failure and not a pass. It is a question for a person, and it belongs in the queue alongside the evidence the evaluator had.

**Done when.** An indeterminate verdict appears with its per-criterion detail and the evidence, and a human decision on it is recorded.

title: Environment: what is in flight, with per-criterion progress
body:
Active objectives, each showing which criteria are met and which are outstanding. `09-EVALUATION` section 5.

**Done when.** Progress moves while a worker works, without a refresh, and it comes from `criterion.satisfied` events rather than from anything a worker reported about itself.

title: Environment: live updates without polling the database
body:
The window needs to change as work happens. Server-sent events from the control plane, or polling it at a sane interval. Not a database connection.

**Done when.** Two windows open on the same objective show the same thing within a second of an event being appended.

**Watch for.** Reaching for a websocket layer or a message broker. `CLAUDE.md` forbids adding one, and the control plane already knows when it appended something.

title: Environment: worker detail
body:
One worker: which objective it holds, its lease and epoch, what capabilities it holds and what it has spent against each, its recent steps.

**Done when.** Fencing a worker's lease elsewhere is visible in the window as it happens.

title: Environment: stop a worker from the window
body:
`01-PRINCIPLES` P13 does not yield: the human can always see, stop and take over. Today stopping is a CLI command. The window must be able to do it too.

**Build.** Revoke a worker's authority, and reach the emergency stop that revokes the root.

**Done when.** A worker mid-objective is stopped from the window and stays stopped, and the emergency stop is reachable in one action from anywhere in the interface.

**Watch for.** Hiding the emergency stop because it looks alarming. It being alarming is the point.

title: Environment: what finished, and was it any good
body:
Evaluation verdicts since the last look, per criterion, with the evidence each one rested on.

**Done when.** A verdict opens the thing it judged: the commit, the file, the remote state that was checked.

**Watch for.** Showing the executor's account of its own work. Mechanical criteria are verified against world state the executor does not control, and the window should show what was checked, not what was claimed.

title: Environment: what it cost
body:
Per objective and per capability: granted, reserved, settled. Read from settlements rather than from anything a worker reported.

**Done when.** The figure in the window matches `maschina cost` for the same objective, to the micro-dollar.

title: Environment: state an objective from the window
body:
Plain language in, objective out. The thing that makes it an environment rather than a viewer.

**Done when.** An objective stated in the window is admitted with a frozen contract and picked up by a worker, with no CLI involved.

**Watch for.** Becoming a chat box. `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 1: a chat box makes the human the scheduler again, because work only advances while they are typing. Stating an objective is one action, not a conversation that has to be maintained.

title: Environment: help a person write a contract
body:
`09-EVALUATION` section 2 hangs everything on the contract, and writing good criteria is hard. The model can draft them from the statement. The human edits and accepts.

**Done when.** A drafted contract is shown as editable text before admission, and nothing is frozen until the person accepts it.

**Watch for.** Accepting a drafted contract automatically. The contract is the agreement about what done means, and a human who did not read it has not agreed to anything.

title: Environment: the activity heatmap
body:
Events by day, the shape GitHub uses. A projection over the log, which means it can be deleted and rebuilt and can never disagree with the record.

**Done when.** The heatmap matches a direct count of events per day, and deleting every projection and rebuilding leaves it identical.

title: Environment: stats, levels and scores
body:
Objectives completed, criteria satisfied, effects performed, denials recorded, spend against budget, null steps survived. A fold over the log, like every other projection.

**Done when.** Every number traces to events, and none of it is stored anywhere that could drift.

**Watch for.** Making it the front door. `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 1: the surface fails if it becomes a dashboard you read and then leave to do the work elsewhere. The queue is primary. This sits behind it.

title: Environment: no score is ever visible to a worker
body:
A worker that can see a score it is judged on optimises for the score. That is the null-step problem in a costume: it rewards looking productive.

**Build.** A check, not a convention. Nothing in the stats path may be reachable from context assembly.

**Done when.** A test fails if a scoreboard value can reach anything a worker is given.

title: Environment: the file tree
body:
A worker's working tree, browsable. The same directory the operator can open in any other editor, because Maschina writes to a real working tree rather than a copy of one.

**Blocked on ADR-011.**

title: Environment: the editor
body:
Reverses `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 2's position that Maschina never replaces the editor. That reversal needs `ADR-011` first and must not be reached by accident.

**Blocked on ADR-011.**

title: Environment: a real terminal on the operator's own shell
body:
`ADR-003` section 3.1: the human terminal and the worker execution path are different mechanisms that do not share a code path. Not one call with a flag.

**Build.** A PTY for the human, in its own module, with no path from it to anything a worker can reach.

**Done when.** A test proves the worker path cannot spawn an unsandboxed process, and the two paths share no module.

**Watch for.** A shared helper 'just for path resolution'. `ADR-003` section 3.2 says a shared resolver is exactly where the scope check eventually gets skipped.

title: Environment: git in one place
body:
Status, diff, branch, commit, push, for the working tree in front of you. The operator's git, not the worker's capability.

**Watch for.** Blurring the two. A worker committing is a capability, brokered, recorded and revocable. A human committing is a human committing.

title: Environment: apply the actionable rule to every panel, in writing
body:
The rule is that everything the surface shows must be actionable where it is shown. It is easy to agree with in the abstract and easy to violate one panel at a time.

**Build.** A short document listing every panel and, for each, the action available on it. A panel with no action is either removed or given one.

**Done when.** The list exists and each panel is reviewed against it before it ships.

title: Environment: decide the component source
body:
`DECISIONS.md` records beautifului.dev as the intended source. Before wiring it in, check the licence, whether it is copy-in source or a dependency, React compatibility, and how it behaves under the renderer's content security policy.

**Watch for.** Creating `packages/ui` for a single application. One application needs components, not a component library. The package arrives when a second surface needs the same ones.

title: Environment: keyboard first
body:
The morning view has to be answerable in ten seconds without navigation. That means keys, not clicks: jump to the queue, answer, approve, next.

**Done when.** The three questions of the morning view can each be reached and acted on without touching the mouse.

title: Environment: the window survives the control plane going away
body:
It will go away: a crash, a restart, a port already in use.

**Done when.** Losing the control plane shows what happened and what to do, keeps whatever was already loaded, and reconnects on its own when it comes back.

**Watch for.** A silent empty state that looks like there is no work.

title: Environment: package and ship it
body:
Signed and notarised for macOS to start with. An application that cannot be installed by anyone who is not already running it from source is not a surface, it is a demo.

**Done when.** A build downloads and opens on a machine that has never had the repository on it.

title: Stage 2 gate: confirm more than one machine is genuinely needed
body:
`14-ROADMAP` section 6 sets Stage 2's precondition as "Stage 1 holds; more than one machine is genuinely needed."

Stage 1 holds. The second half does not, today: there is one machine and no budget for another. Building placement before the trigger fires is building for a problem that does not exist, which is how the previous implementation reached fifty-one packages.

**This issue is the gate.** Close it with the reason the second machine is needed, and everything else in this milestone unblocks. Do not close it because the work looks interesting.

title: Stage 2: node registration
body:
A node introduces itself to the control plane: identity, capacity, what it can host. Registration is an event like everything else.

**Watch for.** Registration conferring authority. A registered node is a place work can run, not a thing that holds power.

title: Stage 2: node identity, persisted and self-generated
body:
An Ed25519 keypair generated on first start, persisted, with the public key submitted at registration. Outcomes are signed so any party can verify them without a shared secret.

**Salvage.** Both previous projects built this. The cleanest version is the old Maschina's `services/node/src/identity.rs`, 94 lines. Read it, then write it in TypeScript against the invariants.

title: Stage 2: heartbeat and liveness
body:
A node reports that it is alive and how many workers it is running. Silence is information: a node that stops reporting has its leases expire and its work fenced.

**Salvage.** Old Maschina `services/node/src/heartbeat.rs`.

title: Stage 2: drain a node
body: Stop giving a node new work, let what it holds finish, then remove it. The graceful half of node removal, and the one that has to exist before the ungraceful half is safe.

title: Stage 2: a node that vanishes
body: The ungraceful half. Leases expire, the epoch advances, work is placed elsewhere, and any effect that was in flight is resolved by its effect class rather than guessed at.

title: Stage 2: measured capacity, not declared capacity
body:
Placement is constraint satisfaction and it needs to know what a machine actually has. Measured: CPU, memory, disk, GPU where present, and whether the machine is itself a virtual machine.

**Salvage, and this one is large.** NeoEngine's `core/neoengine/src/hardware/` is 19,503 lines and detects GPUs across Metal, CUDA, OpenCL and Vulkan, with measured rather than theoretical figures. Read it before writing anything.

**Watch for.** Confusing measuring a machine honestly with proving the measurement to somebody else. Those are different problems and the second one is untrusted nodes.

title: Stage 2: per-node resource accounting
body: What each node has spent, held and settled, per objective and per capability. Three numbers, the same as everywhere else.

title: Stage 2: the node dials out, always
body:
Consumer machines sit behind NAT and cannot accept inbound connections. A node opens the connection to the control plane; the control plane never connects to a node.

Already true of what is built. This issue is the test that keeps it true.

**Source.** `archaeology/02-LINEAGE.md` sections 3.6 and 7.5, where the same wall was hit three separate times across two projects.

title: Stage 2: reaching a node that cannot be reached
body:
The consequence of the NAT rule: to reach a service hosted on a machine behind a home router, something has to bridge it. A relay, a tunnel, or a mesh.

**Decide and record.** The three options and their costs are in `archaeology/02-LINEAGE.md` section 3.6. This is a permanent piece of infrastructure and a permanent line item, not a detail to solve later.

title: Stage 2: the isolation boundary is real
body:
`06-NODES` section 5 and `ADR-003` section 3: the worker execution path must be physically incapable of spawning an unsandboxed process.

**Salvage, and it is the best thing in either archive.** NeoEngine's `core/node/src/sandbox/` selects a backend per platform: gVisor, bubblewrap or Docker on Linux, `sandbox-exec` with custom profiles on macOS, Windows Sandbox or Job Objects on Windows, WebAssembly where nothing else is available. Plus static analysis before execution and resource limits.

The old Maschina, by contrast, ran a bare process with three `setrlimit` calls and no network restriction while telling the model it was sandboxed. Do not repeat that.

title: Stage 2: resource limits per execution
body: CPU, memory, time and I/O, enforced by the isolation boundary rather than requested politely.

title: Stage 2: no network from inside the boundary unless a capability says so
body: Network access is a capability, checked at use, recorded, revocable. Not a default, and never something the sandbox claims to prevent while not preventing it.

title: Stage 2: static analysis before execution
body:
Scan a payload before running it. Cheap, catches the obvious, and never treated as sufficient on its own.

**Salvage.** NeoEngine `core/node/src/sandbox/analyzer.rs`.

title: Stage 2: prove the worker path cannot reach the human's shell
body:
A test, not a convention. `ADR-003` section 3.1 requires the two to be different mechanisms with no shared code path, and section 3.2 says the same for the filesystem.

**Watch for.** A shared path-resolution helper, which is where the scope check eventually gets skipped.

title: Stage 2: placement as constraint satisfaction
body: Given an objective's requirements and the nodes available, choose one. A pure function over measured capacity, in `packages/core`, testable without a network.

title: Stage 2: placement suspends rather than defaults
body:
`06-NODES` section 6: no silent fallback. If nothing satisfies the constraints, the objective suspends and a person is asked. It never lands on the nearest node that almost fits.

**Done when.** A proof shows an unsatisfiable placement suspending, with a question naming which constraint could not be met.

title: Stage 2: placement is never relaxed under capacity pressure
body:
One of Stage 2's three proof criteria. Under load the answer is to wait or to ask, never to quietly widen the constraints.

**Watch for.** A 'best effort' mode appearing during a demo.

title: Stage 2: reputation ranks placement, and never authorizes
body:
`11-NETWORKS` section 5. Reputation is a fold over recorded outcomes: leases completed without eviction, heartbeat reliability, accurate resource claims. It is an input to ranking and to what a human chooses to grant.

**The rule that does not bend.** A node with excellent reputation still cannot host a capability whose trust tier it fails. Otherwise reputation becomes a way to acquire authority and `01-PRINCIPLES` P1 is gone.

title: Stage 2: resource pooling across several nodes
body:
One requirement served by several machines that each hold part of the capacity.

**Provenance.** This is NeoEngine's own contribution and has no equivalent in either Maschina. `archaeology/02-LINEAGE.md` section 5. It is a placement problem, not a new subsystem.

title: Stage 2: migrate a worker between steps
body:
Stage 2's headline proof criterion: a worker migrates mid-objective to a different machine and completes, **with identical authority and no special migration code**.

If migration needs its own code path, the claim that all state is in the log was false, and that is a finding worth more than the feature.

title: Stage 2: migration carries authority unchanged
body: The same capabilities, the same limits, the same spend already settled. Not re-granted, not widened, not silently narrowed.

title: Stage 2: the workspace checkpoint makes migration possible
body:
`ADR-004` addendum and the C1 finding: a working tree with uncommitted edits is durable state that exists nowhere in the log. Checkpointing as work proceeds is what makes a tree recoverable when the node holding it is gone.

Already built for one node. This is the same mechanism across two.

title: Stage 2: a partitioned node causes at most one duplicated effect
body:
Stage 2's second proof criterion. A node that is unreachable but still running is the hard case: it is fenced by epoch, and any effect it completed is resolved by its class rather than assumed either way.

**Watch for.** Resolving ambiguity by guessing. `01-PRINCIPLES` P8: record UNKNOWN, suspend, escalate.

title: Stage 2: a policy engine at grant time
body: Rules about what may be granted, applied when a human grants rather than when a worker uses. Checked at use never becomes checked at policy: this narrows what can be handed out, it does not replace the check.

title: Stage 2: the web working environment
body: `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 5 places it here. It arrives if something needs reaching from a machine that is not the operator's, and not before.

title: Stage 2: snapshots, only if projections get slow
body: Marked Experimental in `14-ROADMAP` section 6. A snapshot is an optimisation over a fold, and it is only justified when rebuilding from the log measurably costs too much. Measure first.

title: Standing work: write 17-STANDING-WORK
body:
The architectural gap found by the lineage audit. Everything in Maschina today is an objective with a contract that gets satisfied and is then done. A hosted service has no completion, only uptime.

Needs: a health criterion rather than a completion criterion, a lease that renews rather than one that ends, and accounting per hour rather than per effect.

**Blocks everything else in this milestone.**

title: Standing work: the obligation primitive
body: What an objective is for finite work, an obligation is for work that continues. Stated by a human, bounded by authority, recorded in the log, and endable.

title: Standing work: a health criterion
body:
A contract says what done looks like. A health criterion says what still-working looks like, and it is checked repeatedly rather than once.

**Verified from outside.** Invariant 17 applies with more force here: the check must not consult the thing being checked about its own health.

title: Standing work: a lease that renews for as long as the obligation stands
body: The existing lease and epoch machinery, held open rather than closed. Fencing still applies.

title: Standing work: accounting per hour
body: Granted, reserved, settled, metered against elapsed time rather than against discrete effects. The three numbers do not change; the meter does.

title: Standing work: ending an obligation
body: A person ends it, a budget ends it, or a failure condition ends it. Every ending is recorded and none of them are silent.

title: Standing work: an obligation that fails its health check
body: Restart, escalate, or stop, chosen by policy rather than by a watchdog guessing. The old implementation force-failed stuck runs, which is guessing.

title: Standing work: keep a repository alive
body:
The first real obligation, and the one that makes the product different from a faster way to type: watch a project, keep its dependencies current, keep CI green, and raise a pull request when something needs a person.

This is what stops a project going stale the week attention moves elsewhere.

title: Standing work: run a service on a node
body:
Start it, keep it up, restart it when it dies, stop it when told. `packages/worker/service`.

**Salvage.** NeoEngine's `core/neoengine/src/services/game_server.rs` enumerates game types with RAM and CPU caps, auto-restart and backup intervals. The shape is right.

title: Standing work: host a website or an endpoint
body: The other workload types NeoEngine had: `web_hosting`, `api_hosting`, `storage`. New resource types on existing machinery, not new subsystems.

title: Stage 3 gate: confirm one worker is provably insufficient
body:
`14-ROADMAP` section 7 gates this on Stage 2 holding and single workers being **demonstrably** insufficient. Not suspected, demonstrated: an objective that a single worker could not complete, with the record showing why.

Close this with that evidence and the milestone unblocks.

title: Stage 3: delegation attenuates, only ever
body:
`04-WORKERS` section 5 and invariant 5. A delegated capability is narrower on every dimension, depth decremented, budget deducted from the parent's allowance rather than added to the child's.

**There is never a widening path.** Not behind a flag, not for the root, not for convenience.

title: Stage 3: the attenuation function, pure and tested
body:
`packages/core/attenuation`. Given a capability and a request, produce a narrower capability or refuse. No I/O, so it can be tested exhaustively.

**Done when.** A property test cannot find any input where the output is wider than the input on any dimension.

title: Stage 3: sub-objectives
body: A worker creating an objective for another worker, with its own contract, frozen the same way, and a parent it answers to.

title: Stage 3: the worker tree
body: Who created whom, at what depth, with what budget. A projection over the log, like everything else.

title: Stage 3: depth limits and cycles
body: Depth decrements and reaching zero refuses. A worker cannot delegate to itself, directly or around a loop.

title: Stage 3: budget across a tree
body: Three numbers per capability, and a parent's reservation covers what its children hold. `05-CAPABILITIES` section 3 is explicit that a single running balance double-counts on delegation and loses reservations on crash, which is why it is three numbers.

title: Stage 3: a child that fails
body: A sub-objective that cannot complete escalates to its parent, and a parent that cannot resolve it escalates to a person. Failure travels up, it does not vanish.

title: Stage 3: revoking a parent revokes the tree
body: `01-PRINCIPLES` P3 does not yield: revocation always works. Revoking a capability revokes everything attenuated from it, immediately, with no cached authority surviving anywhere.

title: Stage 3: a tree completes what no single worker could
body: Stage 3's proof criterion. The demonstration, end to end, with the record showing the delegation, the attenuation at each step, and the budget accounted across the whole tree.

title: Stage 3: swarms are trees, not a new concept
body: Many workers on one objective is composition, and it needs no new primitive. This issue exists so that when somebody proposes a swarm subsystem, the answer is a link rather than an argument.

title: Stage 3: no worker type branching, still
body: Invariant 11. Composition is the point at which somebody proposes `if (worker.type === 'coordinator')`. The answer is capabilities plus configuration, and a check in CI that the branch does not appear.

title: Stage 4 gate: the system reliably ships small changes
body: `14-ROADMAP` section 8 gates this on Stage 3 holding and the system reliably shipping small changes. Reliably is a measurement, not a feeling.

title: Stage 4: an idea in plain language, software at the end
body: The medium-term success criterion in `00-MASCHINA` section 9, and the reason the product exists. A person describes what they want and gets working software, with the ability to redirect at any point.

title: Stage 4: the factory works on somebody else's repository
body: Before it is pointed at Maschina. `14-ROADMAP` section 9 requires this ordering and it is not negotiable: a system that can only improve itself has proved nothing about software.

title: Stage 4: tests written before the change, not after
body: A contract with mechanical criteria implies a test. The factory writes the check first, because a criterion verified by the thing that produced it is not verification.

title: Stage 4: the factory reads review feedback as untrusted content
body: Invariant 18. A pull request comment is untrusted whoever's name is on it. Instruction is trusted only through Maschina under the human's authenticated identity.

title: Stage 4: deploys are effects with classes
body: A deploy is reconcilable at best and unsafe at worst. It is authorized, recorded, and resolved by class when ambiguous, exactly like every other effect.

title: Stage 4: rollback is pre-authorized reversal
body: `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 4's class R1. Rolling back to the previous known-good state is a narrow, pre-approved action, and everything wider than it escalates.

title: Stage 4: keep shipped software alive
body: The obligation from the standing work milestone, pointed at real projects: dependencies current, CI green, security advisories acted on, and a person asked when something needs judgement.

title: Stage 4: measure whether it is actually cheaper
body: `archaeology/Q1-RECOVERY.md` set the pattern: measure with honest caveats rather than assert. Cost per shipped change, against doing it by hand.

title: Stage 5 gate: the factory holds on other people's software first
body: `14-ROADMAP` section 9. Explicit ordering, and the most tempting one to skip.

title: Stage 5: a change to Maschina, proposed and evaluated like any other
body: Stage 5's proof criterion. The system proposes a non-trivial improvement to itself, and it is evaluated by the same machinery as anything else, with a human accepting or refusing.

title: Stage 5: Maschina may never grant itself authority
body: The failure mode that makes this stage dangerous rather than merely difficult. Every grant originates with a human, and a worker working on Maschina is subject to exactly the same rule as any other worker.

title: Stage 5: a change to the invariants requires a person
body: `CLAUDE.md`'s invariants and `01-PRINCIPLES` are not editable by the system, at any stage, under any circumstances.

title: Stage 5: the CLI is the surface a worker uses
body: `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 5 anticipated this: the command line is the only surface a worker can operate, which is one reason it is built first and kept complete.

title: Stage 6: withdrawal authority is never granted, at any stage
body: `14-ROADMAP` section 10, stated as an absolute. Recorded as an issue so it is visible on the roadmap rather than buried in a document.

title: Stage 6: write 18-PARTICIPATION
body:
Who earns and how. Three participants, three earning models, the relay cost that never goes away, and the rules that do not bend.

**Trigger:** Stage 2 holds and untrusted nodes are genuinely next. Not before. `plans/DOCUMENTATION.md` section 2.2.

title: Stage 6: verifying work nobody watched
body:
The problem that gates the entire market, and the one NeoEngine answered with a benchmark presented as a proof.

**The finding that should decide what runs first.** Hosting is externally verifiable: anyone can connect to a port and confirm a server is up, continuously, without trusting the host. Inference is not: confirming it means doing it again. `16-PRODUCT` section 5.3.

title: Stage 6: untrusted nodes hold no credentials
body: A machine belonging to a stranger never holds a secret and never receives a capability it could widen. The broker performs credentialed effects, as it does today.

title: Stage 6: a threat model for machines you do not own
body: `12-SECURITY` covers trusted nodes. Strangers' machines are a different problem and need their own section, written before any such machine executes anything.

title: Stage 6: settlement is a network, reached through a capability
body: `11-NETWORKS` section 2. A blockchain is an unusually well-behaved external system: read state, submit a transaction, verify the result, record an Outcome. No special code path, no chain-specific runtime.

title: Stage 6: decide the business shape
body:
Traffic controller or bring your own keys. Recorded as undecided in `internal/DECISIONS.md` and `16-PRODUCT` section 5.5.

**Deciding early is the failure mode.** The old Maschina had seven pricing tiers before one agent run appeared in any log.

title: Stage 6: the E-scale, and what E1 actually requires
body: `10-RESOURCES-AND-ECONOMY` section 6 sequences economic autonomy. E0, full metering, was required at Stage 0 and is built. E1 arrives at Stage 4. E2 and beyond have no date.

title: Repo: enable a contributor agreement before the first outside pull request
body:
Needed before anyone else contributes, not after. A contribution arrives owning its own copyright, and retro-fitting an agreement means chasing strangers who may not answer. One unreachable contributor can freeze the licensing decision permanently.

**What to add.** The agreement text, adapted from a standard one rather than written from scratch, and something that collects signatures automatically on pull requests and stores them in the repository.

Depends on the licence decision.

title: Repo: a public quickstart that works on a machine that has never seen the repo
body:
`README.md` currently says, honestly, "if you are looking for something to use, this is not that yet." When that stops being true somebody has to be able to run it in ten minutes.

**Trigger.** The first person who is not Ash tries to run it.

title: Repo: a glossary
body:
Vocabulary currently lives in `02-CORE` section 6 and `master/README.md`. The term count is about to grow: obligation, health criterion, standing work, provider, renter.

**Trigger.** When explaining a term twice costs more than writing it down once.

title: Repo: back up internal/
body:
`internal/` is gitignored, has no remote, and exists on one disk. `ADR-005` section 4 named it as the largest risk the layout creates, and it is now the only durable record of eighteen months of work across three projects, including material recovered from memory that exists nowhere else.

**Options.** A private repository, an encrypted backup, or a deliberate decision to publish some of it. Any of the three beats the current state.

title: Repo: decide what in internal/ stays private
body:
Some of it is architecture that would be reasonable to publish. Some of it is strategy, archaeology and business shape that should not be. The current answer is all-or-nothing because the directory is ignored wholesale.

Worth a deliberate split rather than an accident.

title: Repo: keep the issue manifest and the tracker in step
body:
Issues are generated from `.github/ci/issues.jsonl` by `sync-issues.mjs`, idempotent by title. If somebody edits an issue on GitHub and not the manifest, they drift.

**Decide.** Either the manifest is the source and edits happen there, or it is a seed and GitHub is the source after creation. Write the answer down.

title: Docs: the master index is missing two documents
body: `master/README.md` indexes `00` to `15`. `16-PRODUCT` was added on 2026-09-09 and any `17` and `18` will need the same. Small, and the kind of thing that silently rots.

title: Docs: a changelog entry style guide, in one place
body:
The rule exists in `CLAUDE.md`: say what is different, not how it works, because the repository is public and a changelog that explains the mechanism is a design document with dates on it.

Worth restating where the person writing the entry will see it.

title: Repo: measure how long CI actually takes, and whether it is worth it
body:
Eight workflows run on every pull request. That is the right instinct for a public repository and it is not free in time or attention.

**Measure before changing anything.** Time per workflow across the last fifty runs, then decide.

title: Repo: dependabot noise policy
body: Dependabot is configured. Decide what gets auto-merged, what waits for a person, and what is grouped, before the volume makes the decision for you.

title: Proof: run the whole Stage 0 and Stage 1 proof set on a clean machine
body:
Everything passes here. That is not the same claim as everything passing anywhere.

**Done when.** A machine with nothing but Docker and Node clones the repository and `pnpm gate` passes on the first try, with whatever setup steps that requires written into the README.

title: Proof: criterion 3 unscripted, on a second kind of impossible objective
body:
`pnpm stall:live` proves it for one shape: a model refusing an impossible request repeatedly. That is one shape.

**Worth testing.** A worker that keeps producing plausible but worthless artifacts. Null-step counting explicitly cannot see quality, and `03-RUNTIME` section 8 admits it. Finding the second failure shape is worth more than another passing run of the first.

title: Design: null-step counting cannot see quality, and nothing yet can
body:
`03-RUNTIME` section 8 calls itself the weakest section in the document and it is right twice over. Counting steps that produce nothing catches a worker circling. It does not catch a worker producing something worthless every step.

`09-EVALUATION` holds the real answer, because criteria being satisfied is the measure that cannot be gamed by narrating. Continuous evaluation exists. Whether it is enough is unmeasured.

**Not a bug.** An open question with a measurement attached, because every step and every score is in the log.

title: Design: the restatement threshold is measured on one model
body:
0.30, chosen from 549 scored pairs of real observations where restatements ran 0.21 to 0.93 and genuinely different observations 0.00 to 0.21.

That is one model refusing one kind of request. It compares wording rather than meaning. Every observation is in the log, so it can be re-measured against real history rather than argued about.

**Trigger.** A second model provider, or a stall that fires wrongly.

title: Design: contract authorship is the bet that has not been tested
body:
`15-OPEN-QUESTIONS` section 5 lists it: that contract authorship gets cheap enough to be worth it. Every objective so far has had a contract written by hand by the person who already knew the answer.

**Trigger.** The environment's contract-drafting issue, which is the first time somebody who is not the author writes one.

title: Security: private vulnerability reporting is on, and untested
body:
`SECURITY.md` points at GitHub's private reporting. Nobody has ever filed one, so the path is unproven.

**Done when.** A test report has been filed and answered, and the response time it implies is written down.

title: Security: review what a compromised model provider could do
body:
`12-SECURITY` covers the threat model. The model provider is a trust boundary that has not been walked through: the local CLI runs with tools disabled, an empty working directory and a replaced system prompt, and the response is checked for tool use after the fact.

**Worth a written walkthrough** rather than an assumption that the containment holds.

title: Repo: the emergency stop should be reachable without the repository
body:
`01-PRINCIPLES` P13 does not yield. Today stopping everything requires a working checkout and a terminal in it.

**Worth deciding.** What stopping Maschina looks like from a phone, or from a machine that is not this one.

title: Capability: separate delete from write on the filesystem
body:
`05-CAPABILITIES` section 6 is explicit: delete belongs apart from write, because the blast radius differs by orders of magnitude and granting them together is a common careless default.

Today the filesystem capability treats them as one set of operations.

title: Capability: network egress, with a host allowlist
body:
`05-CAPABILITIES` section 6: egress deserves particular suspicion, because it is how anything a compromised worker learns leaves the building.

Scope is a host allowlist, a method set and a rate. Not "the internet".

title: Capability: deployment, with approval on every use early
body:
Deploy, rollback and scale, scoped to a target with a concurrency limit. Effect class 2, reconcilable.

`05-CAPABILITIES` section 6 says almost always `approval: every_use` early on, and early means until there is evidence to relax it.

title: Capability: database, where migrations are unsafe
body: Query is class 1. Migration is class 3, unsafe: not repeatable and not verifiable after the fact. They are not the same capability and must not be granted together by default.

title: Capability: the shell, and why it is the dangerous one
body:
`05-CAPABILITIES` section 7 calls it the most dangerous capability there is, because a shell is a general-purpose authority amplifier: anything the process can reach, the command can reach.

Scope is a node, a command allowlist and a timeout, and it only exists inside an isolation boundary. `ADR-003` section 3.1 keeps it on a different code path from the human's terminal, permanently.

title: Capability: secrets are used, never read
body:
`05-CAPABILITIES` section 5. A worker holds a capability to *use* a credential through the broker. There is no operation that yields the value, at any point, to anything.

Partly built for the repository capability. This generalises it and proves the absence of a read path.

title: Capability: payment, and why it stays deferred
body:
In the taxonomy at `05-CAPABILITIES` section 6 and deferred by `11-NETWORKS`. Recorded so it appears on the roadmap as a deliberate absence rather than an oversight.

`14-ROADMAP` section 10: withdrawal authority is never granted, at any stage.

title: Capability: policy is separate from capability
body:
`05-CAPABILITIES` section 9. Policy decides what may be granted. A capability decides what may be done. Policy is evaluated when a human grants; the capability is checked at every use.

**Watch for.** Policy becoming a second authority system that quietly replaces the check at use.

title: Environment: what is every worker doing right now, and under what authority
body:
One of the six questions `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 6 requires the environment to answer.

**Watch for.** Needing a bespoke data path. If any of the six needs one, something upstream is wrong and the fix is upstream.

title: Environment: what changed in the world in the last day, and who did it
body:
The second of the six. World effects only, so the answer is not drowned by decisions.

`03-RUNTIME` section 2 already distinguishes a decision effect from a world effect in code, which is what makes this answerable.

title: Environment: why did this worker decide that
body:
The third of the six, and the one that justifies retrieval recording its losers. `07-CONTEXT-MEMORY` section 1.

**Done when.** A decision opens the context it was made from: what was retrieved, what was rejected, and by how much.

title: Environment: what did this objective cost, by resource
body: The fourth of the six. Broken down per resource and per capability, read from settlements.

title: Environment: what is waiting on me, ordered by consequence
body:
The fifth of the six. Not ordered by arrival time. A blocked deploy outranks an indeterminate verdict on something nobody is waiting for.

**Watch for.** Inventing a priority score nobody can explain. Consequence should be derivable from what is blocked behind the decision.

title: Environment: what would break if I revoked this capability
body:
The sixth of the six, and the one that makes revocation usable rather than frightening. Which workers hold it, what they are doing with it, and what stops if it goes.

`01-PRINCIPLES` P3 does not yield, so the answer must never be a reason not to revoke, only a description of the cost.

title: Environment: a denial is as visible as a use
body: Invariant 14 and `05-CAPABILITIES` section 10. Denials are recorded as prominently as uses, and the environment is where prominence is either honoured or quietly lost.

title: Environment: onboarding, for the first run on a new machine
body: What a person sees before there is any data: no objectives, no workers, nothing in the queue. That state should teach rather than look broken.

title: Environment: window and layout state survives a restart
body: Which panels are open, sizes, the objective you were looking at. Local to the machine, and never in the event log, because it is not part of the record.

title: Environment: a command palette
body: Everything the CLI can do, reachable by typing. Keeps the surface honest, because a palette entry with no control-plane call behind it is a feature that lives in the window rather than in the system.

title: Environment: notify a person when something needs them
body:
The queue only works if a person knows it filled. A system notification when something enters it, and nothing when work is proceeding correctly.

**Watch for.** Notifying on activity. Most of what Maschina does needs no attention.

title: Environment: dark and light, and neither one an afterthought
body: It is a tool people will stare at for hours.

title: Environment: no telemetry, and say so
body: The application phones nobody. If that ever changes it is an event, a decision record, and a line in the changelog, not a default.

title: Environment: updates are verified before they are applied
body: `12-SECURITY` section 7. An auto-updating desktop application is a code execution path into the operator's machine, and it is only as safe as its signature checking.

title: Evaluation: verification strength is recorded, not assumed
body: `09-EVALUATION` section 3 ranks evidence: mechanical, independent, and judgement. A verdict that does not say which strength it rested on cannot be audited later.

title: Evaluation: run it during, not only at the end
body: `09-EVALUATION` section 7. Continuous evaluation exists for progress. This is the rest of it: criteria checked as work proceeds so a doomed objective is caught early.

title: Evaluation: escalate what judgement cannot settle
body: `09-EVALUATION` section 8. An evaluator that cannot decide does not guess and does not fail the work. It escalates, with the evidence it had.

title: Evaluation: measure whether contracts are worth their cost
body:
`15-OPEN-QUESTIONS` section 5 lists it as one of the things we are most likely wrong about: that contract authorship gets cheap enough to be worth it.

Every objective so far had its contract written by the person who already knew the answer. That is not the test.

title: Resources: exhaustion suspends, it never degrades
body:
`10-RESOURCES-AND-ECONOMY` section 5. A budget running out stops the work and asks. It does not silently switch to a cheaper model, shorten the context, or try again with less.

`CLAUDE.md`: no graceful degradation that changes behaviour unrecorded.

title: Resources: attribution across a worker tree
body: `10` section 4. When a tree of workers spends, the cost attributes to the objective that caused it, not to whichever worker happened to make the call.

title: Resources: a budget forecast before work starts
body: Not a promise, an estimate with error bars, from the log of what comparable objectives actually cost. `archaeology/Q1-RECOVERY.md` is the method.

title: Resources: alert before exhaustion, not at it
body: A budget that hits zero mid-objective suspends and needs a person. Knowing at eighty percent is worth more than knowing at a hundred.

title: Security: a prompt injection test suite
body:
`12-SECURITY` section 3. Repository contents, web pages, command output and forge comments are untrusted content, whoever's name is on them.

**Build.** A corpus of hostile inputs run against context assembly, asserting that instruction embedded in content never reaches the trusted instruction path.

**Watch for.** Testing only the obvious cases. The interesting ones look like documentation.

title: Security: walk the threat catalogue and mark what is covered
body:
`12-SECURITY` section 4 lists the threats. Some are handled by what is built, some are handled by what is deferred, and some are neither.

**Done when.** Every entry is marked covered, deferred with a reason, or accepted with a signature.

title: Security: the root capability, and who can reach it
body: `12-SECURITY` section 5 and `ADR-002`. The root is the authority everything else attenuates from. Its custody is the single most consequential thing in the system.

title: Security: the emergency stop, tested on a schedule
body:
`12-SECURITY` section 6 and `01-PRINCIPLES` P13. It is built and proven once. A stop that has not been exercised recently is a stop nobody is sure about.

Two bugs were already found in it: it would not have stopped anything because no root existed, and it did not stay stopped because a helper minted a new one.

title: Security: residual risk, written down and signed
body: `12-SECURITY` section 8. What we are deliberately not protecting against, and why. An accepted risk that is not written down is an unnoticed risk.

title: Security: supply chain, and what we would do about a compromised dependency
body:
Dependabot, gitleaks, CodeQL, scorecard and SBOM all run. None of them answers what happens on the day a dependency ships something hostile.

**Done when.** The procedure exists and has been walked through once.

title: Runtime: timeouts bound a step, not an objective
body: `03-RUNTIME` section 7. A step that hangs is a different problem from an objective taking a long time, and conflating them is how the old watchdog force-failed work that was fine.

title: Runtime: cancellation, suspension and termination are three things
body: `03-RUNTIME` section 6. Each has a different meaning, a different record, and a different way back. Collapsing them loses the ability to tell a paused objective from an abandoned one.

title: Runtime: failure classification decides retry, and authority never retries
body: `03-RUNTIME` section 5 and invariant 10. Transient failures retry. Authority and budget failures suspend and escalate, always, with no exceptions and no backoff.

title: Runtime: what is durable and what is not, tested by killing things
body: `03-RUNTIME` section 10 draws the line. The way to know the line is right is to kill the process at every point and see what survives.

title: Memory: compression, and what it is allowed to lose
body:
`07-CONTEXT-MEMORY` section 7. A long objective outgrows any context window, so something has to summarise. A summary is a lossy projection, and what it drops has to be a decision rather than an accident.

**Watch for.** Compressing away the provenance. A summarised memory that no longer says where it came from cannot be trusted or promoted.

title: Memory: context assembly is recorded, every time
body: `07-CONTEXT-MEMORY` section 1. What went into a decision is part of the decision. Already true for retrieval scores; this is the rest of the assembly.

title: Memory: a second retrieval mechanism, measured against the first
body:
Relevance is shared words today, recorded as `shared-words` in every ranking, deliberately so a second mechanism can be compared rather than swapped in on faith.

`13-ARCHITECTURE` section 6 names `pgvector` first, and a dedicated vector store never.

**Trigger.** Evidence from real rankings that word overlap is choosing badly.

title: Memory: what happens when memory is wrong
body:
A lesson learned from a run that was itself mistaken will be retrieved confidently forever. There is no mechanism today for retiring a memory that turned out to be false.

**Watch for.** Deleting it. The log is append-only; a retraction is a new event, not an erasure.

title: Factory: the loop, written down before it is built
body: `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 3 describes the software factory loop. Building it before the description is checked against what Stages 2 and 3 actually produced is how the last implementation ended up with a daemon nobody could explain.

title: Self-healing: class R0, runtime-internal
body: `08-ENVIRONMENT` section 4. Not repair at all, just correct operation of the runtime: a retry of a transient failure, a lease renewed, a reconciliation completed.

title: Self-healing: class R1, pre-authorized reversal
body: Roll back to the previous known-good state. Narrow, pre-approved, and recorded. The only class that acts without asking.

title: Self-healing: class R2, proposed repair
body: The system diagnoses a cause and proposes a fix. A person accepts it. The proposal and the acceptance are both events.

title: Self-healing: class R3, escalation
body: The cause is unknown or the effect is ambiguous. Stop and ask. `01-PRINCIPLES` P8, and the thing the old watchdog got wrong by force-failing instead.

title: Environment: pick a repository when you open Maschina
body:
Right now an objective names a repository as a string and something has to already hold a capability for it. Opening Maschina should start by asking what you are working on: clone one, fork one, or open a local checkout you already have.

**Why it belongs to the environment rather than the runtime.** The capability model does not change. A repository is still a scope on a capability, still granted by a person, still checked at use. What changes is that a person picks it in a window rather than typing it into a contract, and that the window can then offer objectives that make sense for it.

**Watch for.** Maschina taking ownership of the checkout. `ADR-011` section 3: the working tree stays a real directory that opens in any other editor at the same time, and deleting Maschina leaves the repository exactly as it was. Cloning on somebody's behalf is the first place that could quietly stop being true.

**Also watch for.** A fork being made without asking. Forking is a public act on somebody's account, and `01-PRINCIPLES` P5 wants an Intent recorded before anything reaches the world.

title: Environment: find the projects you already work on
body:
Nobody should have to type a path to a repository they have opened a hundred times.

The tools already on the machine keep a list. Claude Code has one directory per project under `~/.claude/projects`, named after the path. Codex keeps its own under `~/.codex`. Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Aider and whatever ships next all do the same thing in their own dotfile directory. On this machine that is 23 projects, sitting there, already sorted by how recently they were touched.

**Built as a list of places to look, not a special case per tool.** A new one appears every few months, and the difference between them is a path and a naming scheme.

**What it is.** Read-only discovery, across whatever is installed. Offer the projects it finds, let a person pick one, and open it. Nothing is imported and nothing is written back to either tool's directory.

**Watch for, and this is the part that matters.** Another tool's local state is untrusted content, whoever's machine it is on (invariant 18). A directory name is a path, not an instruction, and a session file is a transcript, not a plan. Read the paths, ignore everything else in there, and never let a discovered project turn into an objective without a person stating one.

**Also watch for.** Reading further than paths. Those directories hold entire conversations, and there is no reason for Maschina to open a single one of them. If it ever needs to, that is a decision with a record, not a convenience.

Related to picking a repository at startup.
